pr_title: ReadOnlySequence: Don't leak the flags that are on _startInteger and _endInteger.
pr_body:
Fixes #42999.
Currently the ReadOnlySequence.End has sometimes a flag that causes odd behavior like:  
`GetPosition(size) != End`
`ReadOnlySequence<byte>.Empty.Start != ReadOnlySequence<byte>.Empty.End`  
This causes more odd behavior later on types relying on the ROSequence.

My fix simply removes the flags when we return a SequencePosition in .Start and .End.

issue_context.title: When SequenceReader is completed, it's Position is not equal to it's Sequence.End.
issue_context.body:
### Description
```csharp
ReadOnlySequence<byte> buffer = new ReadOnlySequence<byte>( new byte[50] );
SequenceReader<byte> reader = new SequenceReader<byte>( buffer );
reader.Advance( 50 );
reader.End.Should().BeTrue();// Pass
buffer.Slice( reader.Position ).Length.Should().Be( 0 );// Pass
reader.Position.Equals( buffer.End ).Should().BeTrue();// Fail
```
I don't understand why this test fails, is this intended ?
The documentation tell 
> Equality does not guarantee that the two instances point to the same location in a ReadOnlySequence<T>.  

With this, I understand that, two instance not pointing to the same location can be equals,
but not that two SequencePositiong pointing to the same thing are not equal.

Discussed this with @tannergooding on discord.
comments: When I took a look this morning its because `reader.Position.GetInteger()` didn't have the "end of sequence" flag set, while `buffer.End` did.

Yes, looks like the `SequenceReader` is not the issue here, the `SequenceReader` call `Sequence.GetPosition`  
And it have the same issue:  
```csharp
ReadOnlySequence<byte> buffer = new ReadOnlySequence<byte>( new byte[50] );
buffer.GetPosition( 50 ).Equals( buffer.End ).Should().BeTrue();// Fail
```

I stumbled on this bug again:  
```csharp
ReadOnlySequence<byte> sequence = new ReadOnlySequence<byte>( new byte[1] );
SequenceReader<byte> reader = new SequenceReader<byte>();
reader.Position.Should().Be( sequence.Start );// fail
```
If this is indeed a bug (IMO it is), I would love to try to do a PR if possible.

EDIT: This three line snippet is not a bug and was my fault, I forgot to pass the sequence in the reader constructor.

> I would love to try to do a PR if possible.

@Kuinox thank you for offering. I'm assigning the issue to you.
Thanks, I will try to do the PR over this WeekEnd.

I noticed that my snippet had an issue: 
```
ReadOnlySequence<byte> buffer = new ReadOnlySequence<byte>( new byte[50] );
buffer.GetPosition( 50 ).Equals( buffer.End ).Should().BeTrue();// Fail
```
`GetPosition( 50 )`: I thought it should fail with an OutOfRangeException.
But someone pointed me to this issue:  https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/27751  
And by reading this comment in particular: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/27751#issuecomment-434524454
I think this change needs more discussion? ^^

Currently, the current behavior is:
`GetPosition(size) != End`
`GetPosition(size-1) != End`
`GetPosition(size) != GetPosition(size-1)`

It leads to weird behavior like in my first comment, but it's not a small change as I thought initially.
So I don't know what behavior I should change, or even if it should be changed.

So I made a fix but there are still weird things:  
An empty sequence will have the flag on End but not Start, but both point to the same position.  
If you instantiate a ROSequence with the constructor `ReadOnlySequence(ReadOnlySequenceSegment<T> startSegment, int startIndex, ReadOnlySequenceSegment<T> endSegment, int endIndex)` the End field won't have the flag.  

I didn't found anything that relies on this flag, it would not be better to delete it if it really has no use?
If anything relies on it, I believe it won't work with the constructor

Ok so I found what was the purpose of these flags:  
It allows storing the SequenceType.  
A simple fix is to stop leaking these flags.
I open a PR.

review_comments: could you please add a similar test for `Start`? And one for all positions from `Start+1` to `End - 1` (inclusive) that verifies that they are not equal to `.Start` and `.End`?

When Seek was called with the offset 0, it used SeekMultiSegment.
SeekMultiSegment will loop until it finds a segment with data, then return a SequencePosition with this segment.
So we ended up with a SequencePosition that point to the first nonempty segment, while `.Start` point to the first Segment.
Why is this specific to offset == 0? It's not the case any time currentLength == offset?

When `currentLength == offset` it point to the first element of the next segment, not the current.
Except when it's 0, because we want to point to the start of the sequence.
But I just noticed that because of this, it's difficult to have SequencePosition pointing to the first byte of the Sequence.
